rules: Disease spread is favored by relative humidity of 94–100%.
Disease spread is favored at 24 °C and below.
Young palms under 20 years are more susceptible.
Water movement and inadequate drainage support disease spread.
Wilting spear leaf is an external visible symptom.
actions: Cut and safely dispose of infected trees as soon as disease is confirmed to limit spread.
Use proper spacing, regular field sanitation, and adequate drainage in waterlogged areas.
Avoid alternate-host intercrops listed by the source under disease-favorable conditions: cacao, durian, papaya, and black pepper.
Use organic and biological control approaches such as Trichoderma only under an approved agronomic protocol.
The source mentions trunk injection with a Fosetyl-Al fungicide within 20 m of infected palms; dosage and authorization must come from an accredited authority.

rules: The PCA material identifies young palms as vulnerable.
Poorly maintained palms are described as higher risk.
Dry conditions are described as favorable to risk.
Predators and parasitoids can suppress pest pressure.
actions: Maintain farm sanitation and monitor young palms.
Protect beneficial organisms; compatible cover crops, legumes, and banana may support biological-control activity where locally appropriate.

rules: Decaying coconut and organic material can provide breeding sites.
Characteristic crown damage should trigger field inspection.
actions: Remove or manage decaying breeding material and maintain sanitation.
The source identifies Oryctes nudivirus as a biological-control option under authorized programs.
Use properly managed pheromone traps with bait as a monitoring and management tool.

rules: Wounded or damaged palms warrant inspection.
Storm-damaged palms can be more vulnerable.
actions: Inspect wounded and storm-damaged palms promptly.
Avoid unnecessary injuries and maintain sanitation around damaged material.

rules: Nearby confirmed infestations increase inspection priority.
Visible scale colonies on leaflets require confirmation and response.
Natural enemies are part of integrated management.
actions: Follow current PCA quarantine and movement-control instructions for confirmed infestations.
Use cultural, mechanical, biological, or chemical measures only under the current PCA protocol and local authority guidance.
